text:
mike.ng: Heads-up — after flipping FA v3 for the rtx/ga100 pool last night we see a ~7% p99 bump on short-seq (<=32) tails in prod on a subset of models. Not universal, seems correlated with mixed batch sizes. CI/bench looked fine.

sarah.k: Ugh. Any CPU-side traces? kernel preemption or workspace OOMs?

mike.ng: No OOMs. GPU utils normal. Attaching a single-request perf sample from logs:
```
model=redwood-v2-small seq=16 batch=1 kernel=fa3 throughput=120 tok/s p50=12ms p95=86ms p99=210ms
```

jin.lee: Can you paste allocator/fragmentation stats? Might be workspace fragmentation when small requests interleave with larger ones.

mike.ng: adding dump from allocator telemetry (/var/log/allocator-summary):
```
free_frag_pct=18% avg_workspace=1.6MB tail_allocs=43 last_gc=2m
```

oliver.h: Interesting — 18% frag isn't catastrophic. Could be kernel selection heuristics choosing fa3 path for seq=16 when fa2 would be better for tiny batches. We recently widened the seq boundary in heuristics.

rachel.t: We did change the cutoff to prefer fa3 for seq>=8 to unify codepaths. Maybe that was too aggressive for some GPU families.

mike.ng: Repro on dev with same CUDA driver and model config reproduces p99 jump. If I force kernel=fa2 it goes back to baseline.

bench-bot: Automated microbench results attached: group A (fa3) median=11.8ms p99=205ms, group B (fa2) median=11.6ms p99=190ms. Variance higher for fa3 on A100 nodes.

jin.lee: That smells like a scheduling/preemption difference — fa3 kernels do more small-float ops or different launch configs that upset concurrent CUDA streams. Any differences in stream prioritization after the RTX kernel change?

oliver.h: We changed persistent stream use recently for cache warmstart. Could interact. Quick hypothesis: fa3 has larger workspace -> allocator occasionally does a small compaction which blocks short requests and shows up at p99.

rachel.t: What about quant path? Are these models running int8/4? We saw some bf16 allocator fragmentation earlier.

mike.ng: These repros are bf16. I can toggle quant path in runtime to see.

sarah.k: Also check hetero-gpu scheduling — some nodes are mixed V100/A100 in the pool. FA kernel heuristics might not be GPU-aware in the allocator.

mike.ng: Good point. The repro node was A100 but the pool has mixed hardware. I'll run gated tests on pure A100 hosts.

bench-bot: New run on homogeneous A100 hosts: fa3 p99 drop narrows to +2%. Mixed-host run retains +7%.

oliver.h: So heuristic bug + hetero scheduling combo. Short-term mitigation: revert the seq>=8 fa3 preference or make kernel choice GPU-aware.

jin.lee: Agreed. Also add a cheap perf probe at route-level that switches kernel if observed p99 increases beyond threshold for N minutes.

rachel.t: For rollout: canary to 5% with auto-fallback to fa2 on p99 regression. We have that mechanism in routing service.

mike.ng: I'll open a quick PR to add gpu_family to kernel-heuristic keys and roll that to canary. Also add telemetry flag to log kernel chosen + gpu_family in traces.

sarah.k: Thanks — please include a short note in the RFC follow-up summarizing the root cause and the rollback plan.

mike.ng: Will do. For tracking: I'm creating an incident card and tagging runtime/telemetry for the trace patch.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: mike-ng/heuristics-gpukey -> canary (5%) ETA 12m. :rocket:

mike.ng: thx. If we still see regressions after the gpu-aware heuristic I'll dig into stream priorities and allocator GC triggers.

oliver.h: FYI long-term we should consider a microkernel perf matrix (gpu_family x seq x batch) to avoid heuristics guesswork. Make it a backlog item.

rachel.t: Adding to runtime roadmap: "kernel perf matrix + auto-tuner".

mike.ng: Filed: RFC-FOLLOWUP-205430 — will link once PR is up.
